title.rendered: I Am Complete in Christ: The Gospel For Today

excerpt.rendered: In Christ all the fullness of the Deity lives in bodily form, and in Christ you have been brought to fullness. Not are working toward fullness. Have been brought. The completeness is already yours.

content.rendered:
In Christ all the fullness of the Deity lives in bodily form, and in Christ you have been brought to fullness. Not are working toward fullness. Have been brought to fullness. The completeness is already yours. The waiting is over.

The Gospel For Today | Thursday, July 9, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“For in Christ all the fullness of the Deity lives in bodily form, and in Christ you have been brought to fullness. He is the head over every power and authority.”
Colossians 2:9-10 (NIV)

Today’s Message

Paul writes Colossians 2 to address a confused situation in the Colossian church. Teachers were coming in to suggest that Christ was not enough, that the believers needed to add philosophy, mystical experiences, angel worship, ascetic practices, and detailed observance of religious calendars to truly know God. Paul’s response is one of the most decisive statements in the New Testament. In Christ all the fullness of the Deity dwells in bodily form. And the same Christ has brought the believer to fullness. There is nothing to add. There is no missing piece.

The Greek word Paul uses for “fullness” is plērōma. It is a strong, weighty word meaning that which fills, the totality, the entirety. In Christ, the totality of who God is, is present in bodily form. And the believer, by being placed in Christ, has been brought into that totality. The Greek verb is peplērōmenoi, perfect passive participle: you have been filled and you remain filled. Not partially. Not provisionally. Completely.

This is the most decisive answer the New Testament gives to every gospel-plus religion that has ever existed. Christ plus philosophy. Christ plus the law. Christ plus mystical experience. Christ plus a particular spiritual gift. Christ plus a special diet. Christ plus a particular liturgical practice. Paul says no. Christ is sufficient. Christ is complete. The believer in Christ is complete. There is nothing missing. There is nothing to add. The fullness has already arrived.

The implications for daily life are freeing. The believer does not need to chase the next spiritual experience to be complete. They do not need to find the right teacher, the right conference, the right anointing, the right method, to fill in what is missing. Nothing is missing. The Christ who fills the universe has filled them. The next step is not to acquire more of Christ. The next step is to walk in the completeness Christ has already given. This is what Paul means when he says we have been brought to fullness in Him.

For Gospelbuzz readers, the truth this morning is settling. You are complete in Christ. Whatever the marketing voices around you are selling as the missing piece, the New Testament closes the door. The fullness is in Christ. The fullness is yours in Him. Walk in that completeness today.

Prayer

Father, I acknowledge that I am complete in Christ. In Him all the fullness of the Deity lives in bodily form, and in Him I have been brought to fullness. There is nothing missing in me. There is nothing to add to what Christ has accomplished. I receive the completeness that is already mine in Him. I refuse the lie that I need one more experience, one more teacher, one more practice to be whole. I am whole in Christ. I walk in that wholeness today, settled, sufficient, and complete. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

I am complete in Christ. The fullness of the Deity dwells in Him bodily, and I have been brought to fullness in Him. Nothing is missing. I walk in that completeness today.

Go Deeper in the Word

  • John 1:16: Out of His fullness we have all received grace upon grace
  • 2 Peter 1:3-4: His divine power has given us everything we need
